summary: Invalidate every live session / token of the user
Complete the password reset with the e-mailed token
Provision a user account (HR / super admin)
Exchange a refresh token for a new token pair (rotation)
Logout: revokes the refresh token and the current access token
Login with username + password; returns access and refresh tokens
Start the password reset workflow (always answers 202, never reveals whether the e-mail exists)
Current user profile, roles and permissions
Employee profile: allowed for the employee, their manager and HR / payroll / finance
Update profile fields (HR) - partial update with optimistic locking
Update my own contact details (self service)
Bulk summaries by id (used by other microservices)
Transfer / promote: department, designation, location, job grade
Change employment status (ACTIVE, INACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, RESIGNED, TERMINATED)
Non-sensitive employee summary (used by other microservices)
Company directory (non-sensitive columns only; cached in Redis)
Directory grouped alphabetically with status counts
Managers ranked by number of active direct reports
Headcount by department and status (Criteria API)
Assign the head (manager) of a department
Employees of a department (read model fed by employee events)
Headcount per department ranked with a SQL window function
Organization chart of the whole company as a hierarchy
Apply for leave (validates range, overlap, eligibility, holidays and balance)
Request cancellation of an approved leave (a pending one is withdrawn)
Unpaid leave days of an employee in a month (consumed by Payroll)
My approved leave in a date range
Upcoming approved leave of my team in the next N days
Team leave calendar (manager: direct reports, HR: company / department)
Recalculate balances with the stored procedure sp_calculate_leave_balance and compare with the ledger
Balance transaction history (written by a MySQL trigger)

Run the missing-punch detection now (also runs nightly)

Monthly attendance summary (stored procedure sp_monthly_attendance_summary); used by Payroll
My attendance records (defaults to the current month)
Daily attendance of the team (manager) or everybody (HR)
My attendance calendar of a month (record, holiday, weekly off, leave)
Holidays of a year, optionally for one location / department
Holidays inside a date range (used by the Attendance and Leave services)
Calendar of a year grouped by month
Calculate payroll for the month (concurrent data gathering, engine, stored procedure)
Finalize an approved run: publishes payroll.processed and generates the PDF payslips
Approve a processed run (finance; not the person who processed it)
Current salary: the employee, payroll, finance and super admin only
Assign the first salary of an employee
Earnings and deductions grouped by salary component
Download a payslip PDF (own payslips, or PAYSLIP_VIEW_ALL)
Salary revision history (written by MySQL triggers)
Employee salary summary: current CTC and financial-year-to-date payroll figures (used by Tax and Exit)

Attach a supporting proof (document id from the Document service) to an investment; also used to resubmit a rejected proof
Income tax statement / annual tax summary with the month-wise TDS table

Cycle report: status counts, average ratings, final-rating distribution
Allocate an employee (a percentage of their time) to the project; rejects more than 100 % on any day
Is the employee allocated to the project on a date? (used by the Timesheet service)
Allocation summary of an employee on a date (stored procedure sp_employee_allocation_summary)
Daily entry: books / replaces one line (project, optional task, day)
Weekly entry: replaces the lines of a week (validates allocation, daily totals, duplicates)
Timesheet correction: reopen an approved sheet
Submit a week for approval (first submission or resubmission after a rejection)
Employee work-hour summary (approved hours, billable vs non-billable, per project) - stored procedure
Steps 4-5: complete a checklist item / clearance / knowledge transfer / asset return / access revocation
Step 1: employee submits a resignation (notice period is calculated from the employee record)
Step 7b: payroll processes (pays) the settlement - publishes settlement.processed
Step 7a: payroll calculates the full and final settlement (salary, leave encashment, notice and loan recovery)
Step 6: HR records the exit interview (answers + feedback)
Step 3: HR confirms the last working day (notice waiver allowed) and the exit checklist is generated
Step 8: HR completes the exit - publishes employee.exited (employee status, account, org chart ... are updated by their services)
Upload a document (multipart): allow-listed types, content sniffing, versioning by title + category
Download: owner, category read roles, or an explicit permission; every download is recorded
Documents of an employee that the caller is allowed to see
E-mail settings (host, port, user, mode LOG / SMTP); the SMTP password comes from the environment
My in-app notifications (newest first; unreadOnly filter)
Kafka topics with partitions and message counts, including retry and dead-letter topics
Notification history of everybody (filter by employee / type / delivery status)
Business event history of all services (who published what, when, partition / offset)
Payroll report (payroll, finance and super admin only: it contains salary totals)
Executive summary: independent sections computed asynchronously (CompletableFuture) and merged
Employee joining and exit summary of a year, by month
Employee headcount grouped by department | location | designation | status
Department report: headcount per department (names resolved through the Organization service)
Workforce analytics computed with Java Streams / Collectors (see docs/202611251532-java-streams-guide.md)
Manager dashboard: team, pending leave / timesheet approvals, team attendance, upcoming reviews, team project allocation
Employee dashboard: profile, leave balance, holidays, attendance, timesheets, payslip, pending items, review status, events (9 services concurrently)
